data.name: Title
data.value: Learning path – step 1

data.name: Heading
data.value: Step 1 of 5: The portal asks its sign-in service

data.name: Lead
data.value: The Citizen Portal does not talk to BundID itself. It sends your browser with an OpenID Connect request to its sign-in service (auth server) – only that service is registered with BundID as a service provider and speaks SAML 2.0 with it.

data.name: Request_Title
data.value: The request your browser is about to send

data.name: Request_Intro
data.value: Authorization code flow with PKCE (RFC 6749, RFC 7636, OpenID Connect Core 1.0). Random values are shortened.

data.name: Col_Parameter
data.value: Parameter

data.name: Col_Value
data.value: Value

data.name: Col_Meaning
data.value: Meaning

data.name: Param_client_id
data.value: The portal's identifier at the sign-in service.

data.name: Param_redirect_uri
data.value: The sign-in service sends the browser back here with the code – only this registered address is allowed.

data.name: Param_response_type
data.value: “code”: the browser only gets a short-lived code, never a token.

data.name: Param_scope
data.value: Which data the portal asks for: openid (sign-in), profile, email, bundid (BundID data), buergerportal_api (API access), offline_access (refresh token).

data.name: Param_response_mode
data.value: How the code comes back – form_post: as a form instead of in the address.

data.name: Param_nonce
data.value: Random value; must reappear in the ID token – binds the token to exactly this sign-in.

data.name: Param_state
data.value: Protected state of the portal (return address, PKCE secret); protects against injected responses (CSRF).

data.name: Param_code_challenge
data.value: SHA-256 of a secret (code_verifier) that only the portal knows (PKCE).

data.name: Param_code_challenge_method
data.value: S256: the challenge is a SHA-256 hash.

data.name: Param_prompt
data.value: login: always sign in again – the sign-in service turns this into ForceAuthn for BundID.

data.name: Param_acr_values
data.value: Required trust level (step-up), e.g. STORK-QAA-Level-3 = substantial.

data.name: Param_bpsim_lernpfad
data.value: Only in this student project: the sign-in service shows steps 2 and 4 as explanation pages.

data.name: Param_x-client-SKU
data.value: Identifier of the library used (Microsoft.IdentityModel), for information only.

data.name: Param_x-client-ver
data.value: Version of the library, for information only.

data.name: Param_max_age
data.value: Maximum age of an existing sign-in in seconds.

data.name: Param_Other
data.value: Further parameter of the request.

data.name: Why_Title
data.value: What matters

data.name: Why_Code
data.value: No token in the address bar: the browser later only receives a one-time code; the portal fetches the tokens directly from the sign-in service (step 5).

data.name: Why_Pkce
data.value: PKCE: an intercepted code is useless, because redeeming it requires the matching code_verifier.

data.name: Why_State
data.value: state and nonce bind the response and the ID token to this one sign-in in this browser.

data.name: Why_Broker
data.value: The sign-in service translates between OpenID Connect (inside) and SAML 2.0 (towards BundID) – so only it has to master the SAML checks.

data.name: Continue
data.value: Continue to the sign-in service (step 2)

data.name: Cancel
data.value: Cancel

data.name: TimeNote
data.value: Take your time, but not too much: the sign-in has to be completed within about 10 minutes.
